name: Burg Freundsberg
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Freundsberg overlooks Schwaz: ancestral castle founded in 1122, a 28-metre residential tower with a silver mining museum and a cosy tavern.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fortress Burg Freundsberg rises on a steep rocky outcrop at 675 metres above sea level, roughly 130 metres above the historic town of Schwaz in the Tyrolean Unterinntal. As the ancestral seat of the noble knightly dynasty of the Herren von Freundsberg, its striking and widely visible keep has defined the townscape for over 900 years. Today, the castle complex houses the Museum der Stadt Schwaz, dedicated to the fascinating history of local silver and copper mining, as well as a popular historic castle tavern with a shady beer garden.

History & Architecture

The castle was founded around 1122 by the Herren von Freundsberg; its castle chapel was consecrated in 1176. Facing financial hardship in 1467, Ulrich von Freundsberg sold the castle to the Tyrolean sovereign Herzog Sigmund der M?nzreiche. Sigmund expanded the fortress extensively and utilised it as a ducal hunting lodge. The architectural centerpiece is the five-storey, 28-metre-high Romanesque-Gothic residential tower (Bergfried): its massive stone walls conceal rare late-Gothic wall frescoes, heraldic cycles, and Renaissance wood paneling. Directly adjacent to the tower, mining families constructed the Baroque castle church with fine stucco work and altarpieces between 1634 and 1637. Since 1931, the municipal museum inside the keep has exhibited precious artefacts from Schwaz's golden age during the 15th and 16th centuries, when the town became Europe's leading silver mining hub and financed merchant empires like the Fugger family.

Visit & Getting There

The museum inside the castle tower is open from early May to late October from Tuesday to Sunday, 11:30 to 17:00 (closed Mondays). The outdoor castle grounds and courtyard are freely accessible year-round. Museum admission prices (as of 2025/2026): adults approx. ?6.00, concessions and students ?4.50, children up to 14 years ?3.50; holders of the regional guest card Silbercard receive a discount. The Schlossschenke Freundsberg serves traditional Tyrolean inn fare. Arrival by public transport: ?BB or S-Bahn Tirol to Schwaz station, then by local city bus (line 1) to the Freundsberg stop, or on foot via the historic Schlossweg path (approx. 25?30 minutes uphill). By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Schwaz, follow signs toward Burg Freundsberg / Burggasse; parking spaces are available directly below the castle.

Tips

Climbing the historic wooden staircases in the keep is rewarded on the top floor with breathtaking 360-degree views across the silver mining district, the Inntal valley, and the Karwendelgebirge mountains. Due to historic preservation, the tower is not wheelchair accessible; however, the courtyard and Schlossschenke tavern have step-free access. Make time to enjoy lunch or a traditional afternoon Marende platter in the shaded courtyard of the tavern.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Oktober Di–So 11:30–17:00 Uhr (Mo Ruhetag)
